title: Normalized descent and uniqueness of an ordinary Hom comparison
statement: Let R and S be commutative ring sheaves on small sites, and fix unbounded derived categories in one localization universe [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let T be an additive exact functor of module sheaves preserving K-injective complexes. Suppose a is a natural isomorphism from T applied termwise to the ordinary internal Hom complex to the internal Hom complex of the two restricted inputs [def-pur-hom-complex]. There is a natural derived Hom comparison e whose equation on L and K-injective I is obtained by conjugating a by the canonical augmentations from ordinary to derived Hom and by the exact-functor localization factorizations [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. This equation determines e uniquely. In addition, for any Hom bifunctors H, HU, HV, exact or ordinary functors F,G,V and c:F composed with G isomorphic to V, the componentwise successive-comparison equation is equivalent to equality of the transported composite comparison with the direct comparison. The canonical augmentation is defined by the fixed functorial K-injective resolution and the localization factorization used in derivedInternalHom, not by an arbitrary choice of an isomorphism.

proof.text: On a K-injective target the augmentation is an isomorphism: the chosen resolution map is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives, so ordinary internal Hom sends it to a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Precompose with Q in the contravariant variable and with the K-injective inclusion followed by Q in the covariant variable. Both are localizations. Conjugate the ordinary natural comparison by the invertible augmentations and the exact-functor factorizations. Fully faithful precomposition along their product descends the natural isomorphism. Its component equation gives the required normalization.

proof.text: For uniqueness, precompose with these same localizations and cancel the invertible augmentation and the restriction factorizations. Fully faithful precomposition reflects equality. For the auxiliary compatibility equivalence, compose the displayed component equality with c inverse and cancel its hom and inverse.

lean.statement:
theorem comparison_exists
    {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (S : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules R)] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules S)]
    (T : Modules R ⥤ Modules S) [T.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits T] [PreservesFiniteColimits T]
    (hT : ∀ I : Complex R, I.IsKInjective →
      CochainComplex.IsKInjective ((T.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I))
    (a : ordinary R ⋙ T.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ≅
      ((T.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).op.prod
        (T.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))) ⋙ ordinary S) :
    ∃ e : derivedInternalHom.{u, w} J R ⋙ T.mapDerivedCategory ≅
      (T.mapDerivedCategory.op.prod T.mapDerivedCategory) ⋙ derivedInternalHom.{u, w} K S,
      Normalized R S T a e
